items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I was crazy about him so I said, “All right, I’ll try it.” ... he told me he had played that instrument at one time.

ctx.x: So when did the bass come into the picture here?

Well it’s funny. I was a brass player all the time I was a kid. I wanted to be, my mother started me on piano and I hit a wall about the John M. Williams second book I think. I couldn’t get both hands to pay attention to what they were doing. But in the fourth grade a wonderful man came to our school, Al Benest was his name, and took over the whole music system from high school to grade school. He saw that he didn’t have much to work with because the previous person had been kind of perfunctory and his whole band…

listener and a kind of a sad reader. But by the time I was in the sixth grade I was disappointed that I couldn’t play the melodies. I couldn’t get enough lip to play the high notes so they wouldn’t put me on first. And I complained to the teacher, and he said, “Well let me see your teeth,” you know, and he says, “you may never really get a good trumpet embouchure with those front teeth.” I got a pair of front teeth that stick out a little bit. But he said, “The school owns a baritone horn. It has a bigger…
